prose: The BBC reports China's GDP grew 4.5% year-on-year in Q3 2026, rebounding from Q2's three-year low of 4.3% as AI-driven exports helped offset weak domestic spending. The figure sits at the bottom of Beijing's 4.5-5% annual target, which analysts say leaves policymakers room to act. China's National Bureau of Statistics described the economy as sustaining steady development 'against pressure' with new growth drivers, and the trade surplus is on track to pass last year's record $1.2tn. High-tech sales led the export strength. The outlook is clouded by global trade tensions and uncertainty over AI investments, while weak spending at home remains the structural gap exports are papering over.
highlights: China Q3 2026 GDP grew 4.5% YoY, up from Q2's three-year-low 4.3%
AI-driven exports helped offset weak domestic spending
Growth is at the bottom end of Beijing's 4.5-5% annual target
Trade surplus on track to overtake last year's record $1.2tn
Risks: global trade tensions and uncertainty over AI investment sustainability
Weak home consumption remains the structural problem exports are masking
